item.description: “Brahmin gf sucks me off, problem?”, Lakshay Lakey claimed in response to a DM by a female follower of Tulip Sharma, who criticised him for his casteist and misogynistic messages.

item.title: Rape is normalised within the patriarchal ‘norms’ of Hindu society: IIT Patna professor Dr Priyanka Tripathi’s another research paper storms new controversy
item.description: "The spectacle of cinema depicts a sustained form of Savarna patriarchy in the act of public rape," Priyanka Tripathi claimed in the paper.

item.title: Mob that assaulted journalist Ruchi Tiwari for being a Brahmin at Delhi University included participants of pro-Naxal protests and Hidma sympathisers: What we know so far
item.description: As seen in the viral videos of the Friday incident, among the girls who surrounded and grabbed Ruchi Tiwari inside the Delhi University, was Gurkirat Kaur, the president of the radical left student group Bhagat Singh Chhatra Ekta Manch (bsCEM).

item.title: An election result like no other: How Bangladesh neutralised the agenda of the US deep state, which once carried out regime change operation, and sidelined its puppet Muhammad Yunus
item.description: It is plausible that Yunus, recognising the dwindling support and looming consequences of his failed plans, may ultimately seek refuge in a Western country, where he hopes to escape the repercussions of his actions and preserve his legacy—if one can still be salvaged. With Yunus ageing, the window for his political revival is all but closed.

item.title: Former Leicester MP and anti-India propagandist Claudia Webbe spreads lies again, claims ‘India was shut down in the world’s biggest strike’
item.description: In a country of this scale, even large mobilisations can happen without paralysing the nation. Calling every protest “unprecedented” or proof of systemic collapse is misleading.

item.title: 2026 Bangladesh election witnesses anti-Hindu voting pattern, Jamaat-e-Islami wins big in border areas with West Bengal: Read why this is a matter of concern for India
item.description: Bangladesh Jamaat-e-Islami performed well in several other districts in this region, particularly those connected to West Bengal in India, such as Jalpaiguri, Malda, Murshidabad, Nadia, and 24 Parganas.

item.title: Hindus in Vadodara protest against the suspected sale of properties in Hindu-majority areas to non-Hindus, in violation of the Disturbed Areas Act: Read what the law is and why it was introduced
item.description: The law was introduced by the Gujarat government to prevent the polarisation of the population in communally sensitive areas.

item.title: ‘Dhurandhar dhass gya’: Liberals mock Indian national Nikhil Gupta, who wanted to kill Khalistani terrorist Pannun
item.description: Mocking Nikhil Gupta with ‘Dhurandhar’ jibes, dragging film director Aditya Dhar and NSA Ajit Doval, into their traitorously boorish behaviour, only shows that the left liberal cabal only waits for opportunities, even in matters of national security, to target and attack the ideologically-opposed government.

item.title: No ban on Russian oil, Marco Rubio clarifies the India-US trade deal: Read how the opposition weaponised Trump’s Pressure tactics and spread myths
item.description: At the Munich Security Conference, US Secretary of State Marco Rubio clarified that India has committed only to not increasing Russian oil imports. This "additional" caveat allows New Delhi to maintain energy security while navigating US trade pressures and domestic political criticism.

item.title: Crowd, devotion and inner peace: My experience of the Bhavanath Mela on the occasion of Mahashivaratri
item.description: I was standing a little distance from the temple premises, looking towards Girnar. A few hours ago, this same place was resounding with cheers. Now there was peace. Here I understood the deepest meaning of this fair. The festival is temporary, Shivatva is eternal.
